reading.title: The Skeleton 1: an anatomy teaching session
reading.text: A tutor holds a skull model. The cranium surrounds the brain, cheekbones lie below the eyes, and the jaw bones support the teeth. A skull model shows the eye sockets, nasal bones, and temporal bones. The foramen magnum is a large opening at the base through which the spinal cord connects with the brain. The tutor moves the lower jaw of a skull model. This bone is the mandible; the upper jaw is the maxilla. A separate spine model shows individual vertebrae. The class follows the spine from the neck down. The cervical spine is in the neck, the thoracic spine is behind the chest, and the lumbar spine is in the lower back. The tutor uses jaw bone as a general name, then distinguishes the mandible from the maxilla. A cheekbone lies below an eye socket. A nasal bone forms part of the nose’s bridge, while temple bone is a common classroom label for the temporal bone near the ear. One individual spine bone is a vertebra.

Anatomically accurate manufactured teaching models only; no gore, exposed patient anatomy, diagnosis, treatment steps, readable labels, arrows, logos, or answer highlighting.
